You are annotator `A` (instance `A-ar-p03`) of a research evaluation of a tool that relates Wikipedia citations
to Retraction Watch records. You label citation units by hand under an annotation guide. Your labels will be locked
before any tool output is produced; you are not grading a tool, and there is no tool output to see or to agree with.
Another annotator labels the same items independently; you never see their work.

**Read first, completely:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6e897802-8925-5c74-9e54-d0b75d7ee684/scratchpad/p2c/work/primary/A-ar-p03/ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md`. Its definitions decide every label.

**Your inputs:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6e897802-8925-5c74-9e54-d0b75d7ee684/scratchpad/p2c/work/primary/A-ar-p03/items/` holds one JSON file per article. Each has the article's wiki, title and revision and
a list `items`; each item has `item_id`, `text` (the unit's wikitext, possibly truncated and then marked
`[...TRUNCATED]`), `identifiers` and `records`.

**For every item of every article**, write one label exactly as the guide's section 2 defines it, with one value in
`records` for every record ref of that item. Read the unit text yourself; base each value on the guide's wording and
on the item. Where the item does not let you decide, answer `cannot_tell` and say why in `note`.

**Your output:** one file `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6e897802-8925-5c74-9e54-d0b75d7ee684/scratchpad/p2c/work/primary/A-ar-p03/out/labels-A-ar-p03.json` in the format of the guide's section 4, with
`"annotator": "A"`, `"instance": "A-ar-p03"`, your model name and version in `"model"` as you know it, and
your start and finish times.

**Rules (non-negotiable):**

1. Read and write only inside `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6e897802-8925-5c74-9e54-d0b75d7ee684/scratchpad/p2c/work/primary/A-ar-p03`. Do not open, list or search anything outside it (not the repository, not any
   other path). Do not run git, `uv` or any CITERIFT command. Do not use the network.
2. Put any helper snippet in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6e897802-8925-5c74-9e54-d0b75d7ee684/scratchpad/p2c/work/primary/A-ar-p03/tools/` or run it from stdin (`python3 -I -`), using only the standard library.
   A helper may read and write JSON; it never decides a label for you.
3. Label every item, and only the items given.
4. When you finish, reply with: per article, the number of items labelled, and the number of items with any
   `cannot_tell` value.

1	# Stage 04 evaluation: annotation guide (P2)
2	
3	Pre-registered with P2 `PREREGISTRATION.md` (section 7) and hashed before the draw. It is the historical guide
4	(`evaluation/ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md`, unchanged) with two additions, both stated in P2 section 7: the record field
5	`same_identifier_for_work_and_notice` (section 1) and the record judgment `ambiguous_object` (section 2.3, example 5). Annotators A and B and the
6	adjudicator receive this file unchanged. The executor checks the format of a label, never its content, and never
7	edits a label.
8	
9	## 1. What you are asked
10	
11	Each **item** is one citation unit of one Wikipedia article revision: the wikitext of a reference (a `<ref>` or a
12	list entry of a references section, as the Stage 03 extractor delimited it). Next to it you see:
13	
14	- `identifiers`: the DOIs and PubMed IDs written in the unit, as written (`as_written`) and, when valid, normalized
15	  (`normalized`: lower-case DOI, PMID digits);
16	- `records`: up to a few Retraction Watch records (`R1`, `R2`, ...). A record describes one editorial event about one
17	  published paper: its `nature` (Retraction, Expression of concern, Correction, Reinstatement), the paper's title,
18	  journal, authors, date and identifiers (`original_doi`, `original_pmid`), and the identifiers of the notice that
19	  announced the event (`notice_doi`, `notice_pmid`).
20	- `same_identifier_for_work_and_notice`: the schemes (`doi`, `pmid`) in which the record itself gives one identifier
21	  as both the paper's and the notice's. When it is not empty, that identifier alone cannot tell the paper from its
22	  notice; decide from the unit text (its title, for example "Retraction:" or "Withdrawal:", journal section, year,
23	  pages) what document the unit cites.
24	- `reached_by`: why a record is shown. "doi:... as original" means an identifier of the unit equals the record's
25	  original-paper identifier; "as notice" means it equals the record's notice identifier; "title tokens" means the
26	  record's title words appear in the unit. **It is a search reason, not an answer**: a record shown by title can be a
27	  different paper, and an identifier can be mistyped.
28	
29	You decide what the unit cites, and how each record relates to it. You do **not** decide whether a paper is retracted,
30	whether the record is correct, or whether Wikipedia should cite it. You see no output of any detector; there is none
31	to agree with.
32	
33	Use only the item: the unit text, its identifiers and the records. Do not use the network or other files. Where the
34	item does not let you decide, answer `cannot_tell`; that is a correct answer, never a failure.
35	
36	## 2. The label
37	
38	One JSON object per item; every field is required:
39	
40	```json
41	{"item_id": "...", "kind": "...", "same_work": "...", "records": {"R1": "...", "R2": "..."},
42	 "single_identifier_attachable": "...", "note": "..."}
43	```
44	
45	### 2.1 `kind`: what the unit is
46	
47	| Value | Meaning |
48	|---|---|
49	| `work_citation` | The unit is a bibliographic reference to a published work (article, paper, chapter, book, preprint) as a source. A retraction warning or template inside the same unit does not change this. |
50	| `notice_citation` | The unit's reference is to an editorial notice (a retraction notice, an expression of concern, a correction or erratum, a reinstatement notice), not to the paper the notice is about, even if it names that paper. |
51	| `retraction_marker` | The unit's content about the records is only a warning or template saying that some work was retracted or questioned (for example a `{{Retracted}}` template with its own identifiers), with no reference to a work of its own. |
52	| `other_mention` | The unit names a work without being a reference to it (an explanatory note, a quotation, a discussion of the paper). |
53	| `not_a_reference` | The unit is not a bibliographic reference at all (navigation, formatting, an empty or broken fragment). |
54	| `cannot_tell` | The item does not let you decide. |
55	
56	When a unit contains two references (for example a paper and, after it, its retraction notice), answer for the
57	reference the unit's identifiers belong to; if they belong to both, answer `work_citation` when the paper itself is
58	cited, and judge each record separately in `records`.
59	
60	### 2.2 `same_work`: do the unit's DOI(s) and PMID(s) name one work?
61	
62	| Value | Meaning |
63	|---|---|
64	| `yes` | The unit has at least two identifiers (DOI and PMID, or two of one kind) and they all identify the same work. |
65	| `no` | The unit has at least two identifiers and they identify different works (for example the DOI of one paper with the PMID of another). |
66	| `single_identifier` | The unit has exactly one DOI or PMID. |
67	| `no_identifier` | The unit has no DOI and no PMID. |
68	| `cannot_tell` | The unit has at least two identifiers and the item does not show whether they name one work. |
69	
70	Judge from what the item shows: a record listing a DOI and a PMID as the same paper's identifiers shows they name one
71	work; a record whose original DOI is the unit's DOI and whose original PMID differs from the unit's PMID, with the
72	unit's PMID being another record's paper, shows they do not. Count only identifiers listed under `identifiers`.
73	
74	### 2.3 `records`: how each record relates to what the unit cites
75	
76	One value for **every** record ref of the item:
77	
78	| Value | Meaning |
79	|---|---|
80	| `cited_work` | The unit cites the record's original paper (the paper the event is about): same paper by title, authors, journal and year, or by an identifier that the unit text confirms. |
81	| `cited_notice` | The unit cites the record's notice (the notice document itself), not the original paper. |
82	| `ambiguous_object` | The unit concerns the record's paper, but the item does not show whether the unit cites the paper itself or its notice (for example the record gives the same identifier for both, and the unit text names neither the paper nor the notice clearly). |
83	| `unrelated` | The unit cites neither the record's original paper nor its notice (a different paper, perhaps with a similar title, or a mistyped identifier pointing elsewhere). |
84	| `cannot_tell` | The item does not let you decide. |
85	
86	Several records can concern the same paper (for example a correction and a later retraction of one paper): judge each
87	on its own; all of them can be `cited_work`.
88	
89	Use `ambiguous_object` only when the paper is clearly the one the record is about and only the document (paper or
90	notice) is in doubt; when even the paper is in doubt, answer `cannot_tell`.
91	
92	### 2.4 `single_identifier_attachable`
93	
94	Whether the unit unambiguously cites one work **and** at least one of its identifiers alone identifies that work, so
95	that the citation could be attached to the work by that identifier alone:
96	
97	| Value | Meaning |
98	|---|---|
99	| `yes` | One work is cited, without doubt, and one of the unit's identifiers alone identifies it (for example the title, journal and DOI agree, and the PMID is another paper's). |
100	| `no` | The unit is ambiguous (its text and identifiers point to different works and nothing decides between them), or no identifier of it identifies the cited work, or it has no identifier. |
101	| `cannot_tell` | The item does not let you decide. |
102	
103	### 2.5 `note`
104	
105	Free text, at most 500 characters: a short reason, especially for `no`, `unrelated` and `cannot_tell` answers. It is
106	kept with the label and never scored.
107	
108	## 3. Examples (synthetic)
109	
110	1. A `{{cite journal}}` with title "X causes Y", DOI 10.1/a, PMID 111; record R1 (Retraction) with title "X causes Y",
111	   original DOI 10.1/a, original PMID 111. Label: `work_citation`, `yes`, `{"R1": "cited_work"}`, `yes`.
112	2. A reference whose title is "Retraction: X causes Y", DOI 10.1/notice; R1 has notice DOI 10.1/notice. Label:
113	   `notice_citation`, `single_identifier`, `{"R1": "cited_notice"}`, `yes`.
114	3. A reference to "X causes Y" with DOI 10.1/a and PMID 222, where R1 (original DOI 10.1/a, PMID 111, title "X causes
115	   Y") and R2 (original PMID 222, title "Unrelated topic") are shown. Label: `work_citation`, `no`,
116	   `{"R1": "cited_work", "R2": "unrelated"}`, `yes` (the DOI alone identifies the cited paper).
117	4. A reference to "Z in mice" with no identifier, shown R1 by title tokens with title "Z in mice and rats", another
118	   journal and year. Label: `work_citation`, `no_identifier`, `{"R1": "unrelated"}`, `no`.
119	5. A reference "Withdrawal: X causes Y", DOI 10.1/a; R1 (Retraction) has title "X causes Y", original DOI 10.1/a and
120	   notice DOI 10.1/a (`same_identifier_for_work_and_notice`: `["doi"]`). The unit's title shows it cites the notice.
121	   Label: `notice_citation`, `single_identifier`, `{"R1": "cited_notice"}`, `no`. Had the unit given only "Doe J.
122	   (2015). doi:10.1/a" with no title, the paper and the notice could not be told apart: `cannot_tell` for `kind`,
123	   `{"R1": "ambiguous_object"}`, `cannot_tell`.
124	
125	## 4. Output
126	
127	Write one label file per batch in the format `citerift-stage04-eval-labels/2`:
128	
129	```json
130	{"format": "citerift-stage04-eval-labels/2", "annotator": "A" | "B" | "ADJ", "instance": "...", "model": "...",
131	 "started_at": "...", "finished_at": "...", "labels": [ ... one label per item ... ]}
132	```
133	
134	Annotators A and B label every item of their batch. The adjudicator labels exactly the items listed as disagreed.
135
